title: The Weight of Symbols
text:
Symbols in classic fiction often operate on several levels at once. A recurring object, such as a green light at the end of a dock, can represent ambition, longing and the illusions of the past. Critics therefore tend to examine not only what a symbol depicts but also how its meaning shifts across the narrative.

Yet a symbol gains its force only when the reader perceives it as deliberate. When the author returns to the same image at moments of crisis, the repetition signals that the object carries a meaning beyond its surface. Such patterns reward a reader who notices recurrence, since the symbol becomes a silent commentary on the characters' choices.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what can a recurring object such as a green light represent?
options: A purely decorative detail with no meaning
Ambition, longing and the illusions of the past
The physical layout of a city

questions.text: According to the second paragraph, what signals that an object carries a meaning beyond its surface?
options: The object appears only once in the narrative
The author returns to the same image at moments of crisis

questions.text: What can be inferred about how the author expects the reader to engage with symbols?
options: By accepting every image at face value
By noticing patterns and reading objects as commentary
By ignoring recurrence in favour of plot alone
By consulting only the critics' interpretations

questions.text: The passage implies that a reader who overlooks repeated images would most likely:
options: Identify the symbol's meaning more easily
Miss part of the commentary on the characters' choices
Gain a deeper understanding of the author's intent
Discover that the symbol was accidental

vocabulary.definition: happening again and again at intervals
a strong feeling of wanting something, especially something lost or distant
the act of doing or showing the same thing again
an explanation or opinion that helps the reader understand something

paragraph_translations: Klasik kurgudaki semboller genellikle aynı anda birkaç düzeyde işler. Rıhtımın ucundaki yeşil ışık gibi tekrarlanan bir nesne; hırsı, özlemi ve geçmişin yanılsamalarını temsil edebilir. Bu nedenle eleştirmenler yalnızca bir sembolün neyi gösterdiğini değil, anlatı boyunca anlamının nasıl değiştiğini de incelemeye eğilimlidir.

Ancak bir sembol, ancak okurun onu bilinçli bir tercih olarak algılamasıyla gücünü kazanır. Yazar aynı imgeye kriz anlarında geri döndüğünde, bu tekrar nesnenin yüzeyinin ötesinde bir anlam taşıdığına işaret eder. Bu tür örüntüler, tekrarları fark eden okuru ödüllendirir; çünkü sembol, karakterlerin seçimleri üzerine sessiz bir yoruma dönüşür.
